title: A uniform principal localization kills the generic torsion kernel
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with B an A-algebra. Let K be a field with an A-algebra structure, K' a field with compatible K- and A-algebra structures, r a natural number, and L_j fields with K'-algebra structures for j in Fin(r). Fix a K'-algebra equivalence e from the quotient of (K tensor_A B) tensor_K K' by its nilradical onto the product of the L_j. Here the nilradical is the ideal of nilpotent elements. Assume B is a finite A-module [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft] and K a fraction field of A. Let R0 be a Noetherian domain with compatible maps A to R0 to K' making K' a fraction field of R0. There exists nonzero t in R0 such that, for every s divisible by t and every principal localization R=R0[1/s] in the universe of A, with compatible maps A to R0 to R to K' and K' a fraction field of R, and every compatible R-algebra structure on the L_j, every R-algebra homomorphism f from (B tensor_A R) modulo its nilradical to the product of the L_j is injective if it is compatible. Call f compatible when for every b in B its value on the class of b tensor 1 is e of the class of (1 tensor b) tensor 1.

proof.text: Apply the generic tensor nilpotence annihilator theorem to A, B, R0, and K' to obtain one nonzero t making every generically nilpotent tensor over R0 nilpotent after multiplication by 1 tensor t.

For each s divisible by t and each R=R0[1/s], use tensor commutativity, cancelBaseChange.symm, and tensor commutativity again to construct the ring equivalence psi:B tensor_A K' to (K tensor_A B) tensor_K K'. It sends b tensor c to (1 tensor b) tensor c. Let m be the tensor map from B tensor_A R to B tensor_A K'. Tensor induction proves f(q(x))=e(q(psi(m(x)))). For a pure tensor, factor b tensor c as (b tensor 1)(1 tensor c), apply the assumed compatibility to the first factor, and apply f.commutes and e.commutes plus the R to K' scalar tower to the second factor.

To prove injectivity, it suffices to test elements mapping to zero. Lift such an element to a tensor y by quotient surjectivity. The compatibility identity and injectivity of e imply q(psi(m(y)))=0. The quotient criterion says psi(m(y)) is nilpotent, and the injective ring equivalence psi reflects nilpotence, so m(y) is nilpotent. Apply generic tensor nilpotence descent to t, s, R, and y. Thus y is nilpotent, and its quotient class is zero. The argument uses neither a nonempty field product nor nontriviality of B.
